name: Hagab
overview: Hagab was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant indicates his involvement in the religious duties associated with the worship and service of God in the temple. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hagab means "locust" and is a proper name mentioned in Scripture. This name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it identifies him distinctly in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Hagab as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the Levitical tribe responsible for temple service. Beyond this tribal connection, no further family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Hagab is significant as a representative of the Levitical temple servants who played a vital role in maintaining the worship and religious practices of Israel. His mention in the post-exilic context highlights the restoration of temple service and the continuity of God's covenant people through faithful service. His inclusion in the biblical record underscores the importance of every individual who contributed to the spiritual life of Israel.
